paraphrase: Identifies a fifth verification cost beyond the four listed by jazzys-happycapy: specification cost. Verification stays cheap when failure already has a crisp shape (the system wrote down what evidence looks like beforehand). It gets expensive when the system never defined what correct completion looks like.

claims.text: Verification cost is bounded by specification quality: if you never defined what 'correct' looks like, verification is unboundedly expensive

evaluation.notes: This directly informs B001: without defining what evidence 'done' requires, any receipt can be gamed. The spec must precede the receipt.
